---
title: "Introduction to taxodist"
subtitle: "Retrieve ordered taxonomic lineages and compare hierarchy nodes in R, Python, or Julia."
---

## What is taxodist?

`taxodist` compares taxa through their positions in a taxonomic classification. Given a scientific name or a Taxonomicon numeric ID, it retrieves the corresponding ordered lineage from [The Taxonomicon](http://taxonomicon.taxonomy.nl).

You can then use those lineages to:

- calculate the distance between two hierarchy nodes;
- identify their most recent common ancestor (MRCA);
- construct pairwise distance matrices for communities;
- inspect shared and divergent portions of lineages;
- test or filter clade membership;
- perform hierarchical clustering and principal coordinates analysis (PCoA);
- save retrieved lineages for later reuse.

Names at different taxonomic levels are accepted. Examples include `"Tyrannosaurus"`, `"Tyrannosaurus rex"`, `"Dinosauria"`, `"Homo sapiens"`, and `"Drosophilidae"`.

::: {.callout-note title="Terminology"}
Throughout this site, **distance** means distance between nodes in a taxonomic hierarchy. It does not mean phylogenetic branch length or elapsed evolutionary time.
:::

## The distance definition

For two ordered lineages, the MRCA is the final node in their continuous common prefix. The metric is

$$
d(A,B)=
\begin{cases}
0, & \text{if the complete lineages of } A \text{ and } B \text{ are identical}, \\
\dfrac{1}{\operatorname{depth}(\operatorname{MRCA}(A,B))}, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

The root has depth 1. Consequently, distinct nodes sharing only that root have distance 1, while a deeper MRCA produces a smaller positive value.

Zero is reserved for identical hierarchy nodes. If one queried node is an ancestor of the other, their distance remains positive. Use `is_member()` when your question is about containment and `taxo_path()` when you want to inspect the route between nodes.

Within a connected hierarchy, this definition is an ultrametric. If two lineages share no root, their distance is infinite. If a lineage cannot be retrieved, the corresponding values are missing (`NA` in R and `NaN` in Python or Julia matrices).

::: {.callout-warning title="Interpretation"}
Classification depth depends on the source and on which intermediate clades it records. These distances must not be interpreted as genetic divergence, morphological difference, evolutionary time, or phylogenetic branch length.
:::

## Installation

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

Install the released package from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("taxodist")
library(taxodist)
```

Install the development version from GitHub:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("rodrigosqrt3/taxodist")
```

### Python

Install the released package from PyPI:

```bash
pip install taxodist
```

Then import it:

```python
import taxodist as td
```

Install the development version from GitHub:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/rodrigosqrt3/taxodist-py.git
```

### Julia

Install the registered package from the Julia General registry:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add("Taxodist")
```

Then load it:

```julia
using Taxodist
```

Install the development version from GitHub:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/rodrigosqrt3/taxodist-jl")
```

:::

## Retrieve a lineage

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
lineage <- get_lineage("Tyrannosaurus")
lineage
length(lineage)
```

### Python

```python
lineage = td.get_lineage("Tyrannosaurus")
lineage
len(lineage)
```

### Julia

```julia
lineage = get_lineage("Tyrannosaurus")
lineage
length(lineage)
```

:::

The returned character vector, Python list, or Julia vector is ordered from the root to the queried node. Retrieval results are cached automatically during the session.

You can also query a known numeric Taxonomicon ID directly:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
get_lineage_by_id("50841")
get_lineage("50841")
```

### Python

```python
td.get_lineage_by_id("50841")
td.get_lineage("50841")
```

### Julia

```julia
get_lineage_by_id("50841")
get_lineage("50841")
```

:::

## Compare two taxa

### Taxonomic distance

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R

```r
result <- taxo_distance("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
result

result$distance
result$mrca
result$mrca_depth
result$depth_a
result$depth_b
```

#### Python

```python
result = td.taxo_distance("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
result

result["distance"]
result["mrca"]
result["mrca_depth"]
result["depth_a"]
result["depth_b"]
```

#### Julia

```julia
result = taxo_distance("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
result

result.distance
result.mrca
result.mrca_depth
result.depth_a
result.depth_b
```

:::

Examples on this site do not hard-code live distances or lineage depths. The Taxonomicon is an external, curated source, so classifications may change over time. Accessing the returned fields keeps the workflow valid when the source is updated.

### Most recent common ancestor

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R

```r
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Homo")
```

#### Python

```python
td.mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
td.mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
td.mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Homo")
```

#### Julia

```julia
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor")
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
mrca("Tyrannosaurus", "Homo")
```

:::

### Shared lineage and path

`shared_clades()` returns the common trunk from the root through the MRCA. `taxo_path()` returns the route from the first node to the MRCA and then to the second node.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R

```r
shared_clades("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
compare_lineages("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")

path <- taxo_path("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
path
```

#### Python

```python
td.shared_clades("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
td.compare_lineages("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")

path = td.taxo_path("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
path
```

#### Julia

```julia
shared_clades("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
compare_lineages("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")

path = taxo_path("Tyrannosaurus", "Triceratops")
path
```

:::

## Work with multiple taxa

Before analyzing a large set, inspect name coverage and resolve ambiguous or missing taxa. Each previously unseen taxon may require a network request; repeated retrievals use the session cache.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
taxa <- c(
  "Tyrannosaurus",
  "Velociraptor",
  "Triceratops",
  "Brachiosaurus",
  "Homo sapiens",
  "Panthera leo"
)

coverage <- check_coverage(taxa)
distances <- distance_matrix(taxa)

coverage
distances
as.matrix(distances)
```

### Python

```python
taxa = [
    "Tyrannosaurus",
    "Velociraptor",
    "Triceratops",
    "Brachiosaurus",
    "Homo sapiens",
    "Panthera leo",
]

coverage = td.check_coverage(taxa)
distances = td.distance_matrix(taxa)

coverage
distances
```

### Julia

```julia
taxa = [
    "Tyrannosaurus",
    "Velociraptor",
    "Triceratops",
    "Brachiosaurus",
    "Homo sapiens",
    "Panthera leo",
]

coverage = check_coverage(taxa)
distances = distance_matrix(taxa)

coverage
distances
Matrix(distances)
distances["Tyrannosaurus", "Velociraptor"]
```

:::

In R, `distance_matrix()` returns a base `dist` object. Convert it with `as.matrix()` when a full square matrix is required. Python returns a symmetric `pandas.DataFrame`. Julia returns a `TaxonomicDistanceMatrix` supporting both integer and taxon-label indexing.

Taxa that cannot be resolved remain represented in the result, with missing pairwise distances.

### Distances from one focal taxon

`focal_distances()` includes the MRCA and its depth for every comparison. `closest_relative()` provides the simpler taxon-and-distance view.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### R

```r
community <- c(
  "Velociraptor",
  "Triceratops",
  "Brachiosaurus",
  "Homo sapiens"
)

focal_distances("Tyrannosaurus", community)
closest_relative("Tyrannosaurus", community)
```

#### Python

```python
community = [
    "Velociraptor",
    "Triceratops",
    "Brachiosaurus",
    "Homo sapiens",
]

td.focal_distances("Tyrannosaurus", community)
td.closest_relative("Tyrannosaurus", community)
```

#### Julia

```julia
community = [
    "Velociraptor",
    "Triceratops",
    "Brachiosaurus",
    "Homo sapiens",
]

focal_distances("Tyrannosaurus", community)
closest_relative("Tyrannosaurus", community)
```

:::

## Test and filter clade membership

Clade matching is exact, case-insensitive, and ignores surrounding whitespace. A partial string such as `"Dino"` does not match `"Dinosauria"`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
is_member("Tyrannosaurus", "Theropoda")
is_member("Triceratops", "Theropoda")

filter_clade(taxa, "Dinosauria")
```

### Python

```python
td.is_member("Tyrannosaurus", "Theropoda")
td.is_member("Triceratops", "Theropoda")

td.filter_clade(taxa, "Dinosauria")
```

### Julia

```julia
is_member("Tyrannosaurus", "Theropoda")
is_member("Triceratops", "Theropoda")

filter_clade(taxa, "Dinosauria")
```

:::

## Clustering, ordination, and heatmaps

The analysis helpers accept taxon names or a previously computed distance object.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
distances <- distance_matrix(taxa)

cluster <- taxo_cluster(distances)
ordination <- taxo_ordinate(distances, k = 2)

plot(cluster)
summary(ordination)
plot(ordination)
taxo_heatmap(distances)
```

### Python

```python
distances = td.distance_matrix(taxa)

cluster = td.taxo_cluster(distances)
ordination = td.taxo_ordinate(distances, k=2)
heatmap_data = td.taxo_heatmap(distances)
```

### Julia

```julia
distances = distance_matrix(taxa)

cluster = taxo_cluster(distances)
ordination = taxo_ordinate(distances, k=2)

plot_taxodist_cluster(cluster)
summary_taxodist_ord(ordination)
plot_taxodist_ord(ordination)
taxo_heatmap(distances)
```

:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Check the matrix first"}
Clustering, ordination, and heatmaps require at least two taxa and a finite, complete distance matrix. The helpers warn and return an empty analysis component when the matrix contains missing or infinite distances.
:::

The clustering dendrogram is a visualization of taxonomic hierarchy distances. It is not a phylogeny inferred from characters, sequences, or branch lengths.

## Coverage, search, and homonyms

Use `check_coverage()` before a large calculation to identify names that cannot be resolved. Use `taxo_search()` to inspect possible Taxonomicon matches when a name is ambiguous or unexpected.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
check_coverage(c("Tyrannosaurus", "Homo sapiens", "Fakeosaurus"))
taxo_search("Bacteria")
get_taxonomicon_id("Tyrannosaurus")
```

### Python

```python
td.check_coverage(["Tyrannosaurus", "Homo sapiens", "Fakeosaurus"])
td.taxo_search("Bacteria")
td.get_taxonomicon_id("Tyrannosaurus")
```

### Julia

```julia
check_coverage(["Tyrannosaurus", "Homo sapiens", "Fakeosaurus"])
taxo_search("Bacteria")
get_taxonomicon_id("Tyrannosaurus")
```

:::

When reproducibility matters, record the resolved numeric ID and the retrieval date. This helps distinguish homonyms and documents which external classification was queried.

## Save and restore the cache

Retrieved identifiers and lineages are cached in memory. Saving the cache avoids repeating those network requests in a later session.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
cache_info()
save_cache("taxodist-cache.rds")

clear_cache()
load_cache("taxodist-cache.rds")
```

### Python

```python
td.cache_info()
td.save_cache("taxodist-cache.pkl")

td.clear_cache()
td.load_cache("taxodist-cache.pkl")
```

### Julia

```julia
cache_info()
save_cache("taxodist-cache.json")

clear_cache()
load_cache("taxodist-cache.json")
```

:::

The three implementations use language-specific cache formats: `.rds` in R, `.pkl` in Python, and `.json` in Julia. These cache files are not interchangeable. Python cache files use `pickle`; only load them from sources you trust.

## Use the offline reference data

The packaged `taxobase` object provides a fixed, offline dataset for examples, tests, and comparisons that must not depend on the availability or current state of The Taxonomicon.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```r
data(taxobase, package = "taxodist")
names(taxobase)
taxobase$metadata
```

### Python

```python
taxobase = td.load_taxobase()
taxobase.keys()
taxobase["metadata"]
```

### Julia

```julia
taxobase = load_taxobase()
keys(taxobase)
taxobase.metadata
```

:::

Release 0.6.0 distributes equivalent reference content in all three packages, preserving component names, taxon order, matrices, examples, and provenance metadata. The native package objects remain language-specific.

## Data source and citation

All live lineage data originate from The Taxonomicon, based on *Systema Naturae 2000*:

> Brands, S.J. (1989 onwards). *Systema Naturae 2000*. Amsterdam, The Netherlands. Retrieved from The Taxonomicon, <http://taxonomicon.taxonomy.nl>.

Published analyses should cite both the `taxodist` software and the underlying classification source.
